facts.statement: Fossils of Spinosaurus mirabilis were collected in Niger during excavations in 2000, 2019, and 2022 led by Paul Sereno.
facts.quote: Fossils of Spinosaurus mirabilis were collected from outcrops of the Farak Formation of Niger during a series of excavations in 2000, 2019, and 2022, led by paleontologist Paul Sereno.

facts.statement: Fossils of Spinosaurus mirabilis were found at two localities named Iguidi and Jenguebi.
facts.quote: Material was collected from two localities, Iguidi and Jenguebi.

facts.statement: Spinosaurus mirabilis was formally described as a new species in 2026 by Sereno and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2026, Sereno and colleagues described Spinosaurus mirabilis as a new species of the genus Spinosaurus based on these fossil remains.

facts.statement: The species was formally described by a team led by Paul Sereno in a study published in Science on February 19, 2026.
facts.quote: Fue descrita formalmente por un equipo liderado por el estadounidense profesorado a la paleontología Paul Callistus Sereno, en un estudio publicado en la revista científica Science el día Jueves 19 de febrero de 2026.

facts.statement: Spinosaurus mirabilis lived during the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian) period.
facts.quote: Age: Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian)

facts.statement: The species lived approximately 95 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian).
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico Tardío durante a finales de la edad del Cenomaniense, hace aproximadamente 95 millones de años.

facts.statement: Spinosaurus mirabilis is known from the Farak Formation in Niger.
facts.quote: known from the Late Cretaceous Farak Formation of Niger.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in a Cenomanian-aged fluvial system composed of sandstone and sandy shale.
facts.quote: The remains of S. mirabilis were unearthed from the Farak Formation, characterized by sandstone and sandy shale, representing a Cenomanian-aged fluvial system.

facts.statement: A unique trait is a distinctive pointed crest with a scimitar shape formed by the nasal and prefrontal bones.
facts.quote: One of the most unique traits of S. mirabilis is its distinctive pointed crest with a superficial scimitar-shape, formed by the nasal and prefrontal bones.

facts.statement: The holotype, a subadult individual, is estimated to have reached a full body length of around 8 meters.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, which belongs to a subadult individual, was estimated to have a full body length of around 8 m.

facts.statement: Spinosaurus mirabilis is classified as a spinosaurid theropod and a species of Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: Notes: A spinosaurid theropod; a species of Spinosaurus.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis recovered Spinosaurus mirabilis as the sister group to Spinosaurus aegyptiacus.
facts.quote: They consistently recovered the Nigerian taxon as the sister group to the better-known Spinosaurus aegyptiacus, supporting their assignment to the same genus.

facts.statement: The species belongs to the family Spinosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Spinosauridae

facts.statement: The species belongs to the subfamily Spinosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Spinosaurinae

facts.statement: The species belongs to the tribe Spinosaurini.
facts.quote: tribus: Spinosaurini

facts.statement: It is debated whether certain fossils initially assigned to Carcharodontosaurus actually belong to a spinosaurid, as some cervical vertebrae were erroneously referred to C. saharicus.
facts.quote: MNBH IGU11, an anterior dorsal centrum, was initially identified as a mid-cervical centrum and referred to the coeval carcharodontosaurid Carcharodontosaurus iguidensis due to its similarities to cervical vertebrae erroneously referred to C. saharicus, which actually come from a spinosaurid.

facts.statement: The most diagnostic fossils of Spinosaurus mirabilis come from the Jenguebi locality, excavated between 2019 and 2022 under the direction of Paul Sereno.
facts.quote: Los fósiles más diagnósticos de Spinosaurus mirabilis proceden del yacimiento de la Localidad de Jenguebi, durante las excavaciones de los años 2019 y 2022, dirigidas por Paul Sereno

facts.statement: Since its 2026 description, the Jenguebi materials are housed at the Abdou Moumouni University in Niger.
facts.quote: A partir de su descripción en 2026, los materiales recuperados en Jenguebi se encuentran conservados en la Universidad Abdou Moumouni en Níger

facts.statement: Fossils found in Iguidi are temporarily on loan to Paul Sereno's fossil laboratory at the University of Chicago.
facts.quote: mientras que los fósiles encontrados en Iguidi se encuentran temporalmente en préstamo al laboratorio de fósiles de Sereno en la Universidad de Chicago

facts.statement: Spinosaurus mirabilis lived during the Cenomanian stage, between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The fossils were found in an interior basin of the central Sahara within the Farak Formation.
facts.quote: dentro de una cuenca interior del Sáhara central, en la Formación Farak

facts.statement: The strata containing these fossils are of the same age as those where Spinosaurus aegyptiacus remains have been found.
facts.quote: Los estratos que los contenían son equivalentes en edad a aquellos donde se han encontrado restos de Spinosaurus aegyptiacus

facts.statement: Unlike S. aegyptiacus, the new S. mirabilis specimens were found in interior fluvial deposits rather than coastal sediments.
facts.quote: a diferencia de estos, los nuevos ejemplares fueron hallados en depósitos fluviales interiores y no en sedimentos costeros

facts.statement: According to Sereno et al. (2026), the holotype specimen of Spinosaurus mirabilis has a total body length of 8 meters.
facts.quote: En el trabajo de Sereno Et al. (2026) mencionan en su diagrama esquelético de Spinosaurus mirabilis que su longitud corporal para el ejemplar holotipo es de 8 metros en total

facts.statement: Researchers suggest a hypothetical fully mature individual could have reached 10 to 14 meters in length.
facts.quote: En el trabajo sugieren que un individuo completamente maduro hipotético podría haber alcanzado a los 10 - 14 metros de largo

facts.statement: The species features a hypertrophied, high nasal-prefrontal crest shaped like a scimitar with a height of 50 cm.
facts.quote: Cresta nasal-prefrontal hipertrofiada y alta, con forma de cimitarra con una altura de 50 cm

facts.statement: The cranial crest, likely covered in keratin during life, suggests a function related to visual display or intraspecific recognition.
facts.quote: La cresta craneal, probablemente recubierta de queratina en vida, sugiere una función relacionada con la exhibición visual o el reconocimiento intraespecífico

facts.statement: The discovery of S. mirabilis in interior fluvial sediments supports a predominantly riparian lifestyle.
facts.quote: El hallazgo de S. mirabilis en sedimentos fluviales interiores aporta evidencia a favor de un estilo de vida predominantemente ribereño

facts.statement: It is interpreted that Spinosaurus mirabilis was a wading hunter capable of moving through shallow waters while ambushing aquatic prey in rivers and margins.
facts.quote: En consecuencia, se interpreta que Spinosaurus mirabilis habría sido un cazador zancudo, capaz de desplazarse por aguas someras mientras acechaba presas acuáticas en ríos y márgenes fluviales

facts.statement: Interpretations of the species' lifestyle have oscillated between a semi-aquatic ambush predator and a fully aquatic form with active diving capabilities.
facts.quote: Las interpretaciones han oscilado entre la de un depredador semiacuático de emboscada y la de una forma plenamente acuática con capacidad de buceo activo en busca de presas

facts.statement: Spinosaurus mirabilis is classified as a parent group under Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: Parent group: Spinosaurus

facts.statement: Spinosaurus mirabilis belongs to the family Spinosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Spinosauridae

facts.statement: Spinosaurus mirabilis is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: One specimen found in Iguidi (MNBH IGU11) was previously classified as Carcharodontosaurus iguidensis by Brusatte and Sereno in 2007.
facts.quote: Uno de los especímenes encontrados en Iguidi (MNBH IGU11) fueron clasificados anteriormente como Carcharodontosaurus iguidensis por parte de Stephen L. Brusatte y Sereno (2007)

facts.statement: In 2016, Chiarenza and Cau proposed that several fossils assigned to C. iguidensis, including MNBH IGU11, did not belong to that species but were instead classified as Sigilmassasaurus brevicollis.
facts.quote: Luego, en 2016, Alfio Alessandro Chiarenza y Andrea Cau propusieron que varios fósiles asignados a C. iguidensis no pertenecían a este último, siendo uno de estos MNBH IGU11, clasificado como perteneciente a Sigilmassasaurus brevicollis

facts.statement: The 2026 article by Sereno et al. reassigned the fossil as a potential specimen of Spinosaurus mirabilis.
facts.quote: Y la llegada del artículo de Sereno Et al. (2026) reasignaron el fósil como un potencial espécimen de Spinosaurus mirabilis

facts.statement: Paleontologist Daniel Vidal noted that the holotype remains found during the 2019 campaign were initially mistaken for a dentary related to a non-spinosaurid theropod, specifically a Carcharodontosaurid.
facts.quote: Según palabras del paleontólogo español Daniel Vidal, los restos del holotipo encontrados durante la campaña en 2019 fue confundido inicialmente con un dentario relacionado a otro Terópodo fuera de Spinosauridae, más precisamente a los de un Carcharodontosauridae

facts.statement: Spinosaurus mirabilis is distinguished by a scimitar-shaped bony crest that projects far above its skull roof.
Spinosaurus mirabilis was discovered in the central Sahara in a riparian habitat alongside long-necked dinosaurs.
Spinosaurus mirabilis is described as a close relative of Spinosaurus aegyptiacus, a sail-backed, fish-eating giant.
Researchers propose that spinosaurid evolution occurred in three discrete phases.
